lesson.arabic-b1-source-task.title_en: Comparing two sources: يَتَّفِقُ, يَخْتَلِفُ, مُشْتَرَك
lesson.arabic-b1-source-task.family_en: Keeping each source's points apart, then saying where they meet and part
steps: Keep each source's points apart first: its topic, its main point, and its evidence.
Then compare: يَتَّفِقُ النَّصَّانِ عَلَى, the two texts agree on; يَخْتَلِفُ النَّصَّانِ فِي, the two texts differ on.
A shared topic isn't a shared claim: two texts about learning can answer different questions.
غَيْر, not, turns a describing word round, and the word after it takes -i, here -in: غَيْرُ مَوْثُوقٍ, unreliable.
Two sources agreeing doesn't make a claim true: it shows only that they agree.

examples.en: The two writers agree on the importance of reading.
But they differ on the reasons.

why.q_en: Why يَتَّفِقُ الْكَاتِبَانِ, singular, but لَكِنَّهُمَا يَخْتَلِفَانِ, for two?
why.a_en: A verb that comes before its doers stays singular, even for two or more: يَتَّفِقُ الْكَاتِبَانِ. When the doers come first, as a noun or a pronoun, the verb matches them: لَكِنَّهُمَا يَخْتَلِفَانِ, but they two differ.

selftest.why_en: مَوْضُوعٌ مُشْتَرَكٌ is a shared topic.
غَيْر comes before the describing word, which ends in -in. لَيْسَ would need -an (لَيْسَ مَوْثُوقًا, it isn't reliable), and لَا doesn't make a describing word negative this way.
قَارَنَ بَيْنَ النَّصَّيْنِ: he compared the two texts.

lesson.arabic-b1-explainer.title_en: Explaining something to a listener: شَرَحَ, وَحْدَهُ لَا يَكْفِي
lesson.arabic-b1-explainer.family_en: The question first, a simple example, links between points, and a check

table.en: on its own, it isn't enough

steps: Start with the question you're answering, so the listener knows where you're going.
Bring in only the terms they need, and explain each one simply.
Give one concrete example that supports the point.
Link your points so each builds on the last: وَحْدَهُ لَا يَكْفِي, on its own it isn't enough; أَيْضًا, also.
Check with هَلْ هَذَا وَاضِحٌ؟, then close with فِي الْخِتَامِ and the point in one sentence.

examples.ar: الْحِفْظُ وَحْدَهُ لَا يَكْفِي لِتَعَلُّمِ لُغَةٍ.
examples.en: Memorising alone isn't enough to learn a language.
The teacher explained the rule with a simple example.

examples.ar: فِي الْخِتَامِ، الِاسْتِعْمَالُ هُوَ أَفْضَلُ طَرِيقَةٍ لِلتَّعَلُّمِ.
examples.en: In closing, using the language is the best way to learn.

why.q_en: Why وَحْدَهُ in الْحِفْظُ وَحْدَهُ, but وَحْدَهَا for reading?
why.a_en: وَحْدَ, alone, always carries an ending for whoever or whatever is alone: وَحْدِي, on my own; وَحْدَهُ for a masculine word; وَحْدَهَا for a feminine one. The verb matches too: الْقِرَاءَةُ وَحْدَهَا لَا تَكْفِي.

selftest.q_en: How do you check your listener has followed?
selftest.why_en: فِي الْخِتَامِ closes, and وَحْدَهُ لَا يَكْفِي links a point.
قِرَاءَة is feminine, so وَحْدَهَا and تَكْفِي.

selftest.q_en: What should an explanation start with?
selftest.why_en: Then the listener knows where you're heading.

lesson.arabic-b1-unprepared.title_en: Answering on the spot: دَعْنِي أُفَكِّرُ, يَعْتَمِدُ عَلَى
lesson.arabic-b1-unprepared.family_en: Taking a moment, saying how sure you are, and answering the question asked
steps: Listen for what the question actually asks: لِمَاذَا wants a reason, not a name.
It's fine to take a moment: دَعْنِي أُفَكِّرُ, let me think.
Say how sure you are, or how you mean it: عَلَى حَدِّ عِلْمِي, as far as I know; فِي الْحَقِيقَةِ, actually; بِصَرَاحَةٍ, honestly.
If the answer depends on something, say so with يَعْتَمِدُ عَلَى, it depends on.
If you're unsure what's being asked, check before you answer: a fluent answer to the wrong question doesn't help.

examples.en: Let me think for a moment.

examples.ar: اِخْتَرْتُ هَذَا الْكِتَابَ لِأَنَّ قِصَّتَهُ تُشْبِهُ حَيَاتِي.
examples.en: I chose this book because its story is like my own life.

examples.ar: عَلَى حَدِّ عِلْمِي، تَبْدَأُ الْمُحَاضَرَةُ فِي التَّاسِعَةِ.
examples.en: As far as I know, the lecture starts at nine.

words.en: my knowledge: "as far as I know"

why.q_en: Why اِخْتَرْتُ, with a short a, from اِخْتَارَ?
why.a_en: The long ā in the middle shortens before an ending that starts with a consonant, as in قَالَ, قُلْتُ: اِخْتَارَ, he chose; اِخْتَرْتُ, I chose.

selftest.q_en: Which phrase gives you a moment to think?
selftest.why_en: عَلَى حَدِّ عِلْمِي is "as far as I know", and بِصَرَاحَةٍ "honestly".
هَذَا يَعْتَمِدُ عَلَى الْوَقْتِ: that depends on the time.

selftest.q_en: You're asked لِمَاذَا اخْتَرْتَ هَذَا الْكِتَابَ؟ What does the answer need?

lesson.arabic-b1-independent-cycle.title_en: Planning your own learning: أَوْلَوِيَّة, تَمْرِين, تَدْرِيجِيًّا
lesson.arabic-b1-independent-cycle.family_en: A small cycle you can repeat: choose, practise, check, record
steps: A learning cycle has four steps: choose a text you can mostly follow, find a few gaps, practise them, then check them in something new.
Give a small set of gaps أَوْلَوِيَّة, priority: ones you can fix now, not everything at once.
Practise them with a short تَمْرِين, and keep a سِجِلّ of what you did and what help you used.
Raise the difficulty تَدْرِيجِيًّا, gradually. Easy texts still count.

examples.ar: أَوْلَوِيَّتِي هَذَا الشَّهْرَ كَلِمَاتُ السَّبَبِ وَالنَّتِيجَةِ.
examples.en: My priority this month is the words for cause and result.

examples.ar: أَكْتُبُ فِي سِجِلِّي مَا تَعَلَّمْتُهُ كُلَّ أُسْبُوعٍ.
examples.en: Every week I write down in my log what I learned.

why.a_en: تَدْرِيجِيّ means gradual. Used to say how something is done, it takes -an, like كَثِيرًا and جِدًّا: أَتَقَدَّمُ تَدْرِيجِيًّا, I'm making progress gradually.

selftest.why_en: A record is سِجِلّ, and patience صَبْر.

lesson.arabic-b1-portfolio.title_en: Describing what you can do: قَادِرٌ عَلَى, نُقْطَةُ قُوَّةٍ, دَلِيل
lesson.arabic-b1-portfolio.family_en: Saying what you can do, with the evidence and the help you had
steps: Say what you can do, with evidence: أَنَا قَادِرٌ عَلَى شَرْحِ فِكْرَةٍ بَسِيطَةٍ, I can explain a simple idea. A woman says قَادِرَةٌ.
قَادِرٌ عَلَى takes a noun, often a verbal noun: قَادِرٌ عَلَى الْكِتَابَةِ, able to write.
Give each piece of دَلِيل, evidence, its date and the help you had. Was it مُسْتَقِلّ, done on your own?
Choose your next مَرْحَلَة from your skills as they really are: a تَخَصُّص, a specialism, builds on the common ones.

examples.en: I've become able to understand the news. (a woman)
This recording is evidence of my progress.

why.q_en: Why قَادِرٌ عَلَى الْكِتَابَةِ, with a noun, where English says "able to write"?
why.a_en: عَلَى is followed by a noun, so the action becomes a verbal noun: الْكِتَابَة, writing. You can also use أَنْ and a verb: قَادِرٌ عَلَى أَنْ أَكْتُبَ.

selftest.q_en: How does a woman say "I'm able to explain"?
selftest.why_en: A woman adds ـَة, and قَادِر takes عَلَى.

selftest.q_en: What should each piece of evidence say?
choices: its date and the help you had
nothing: the work speaks for itself
selftest.answer: its date and the help you had
selftest.why_en: Then it shows what you can do, and under what conditions.

phrases_ar: أَنَا قَادِرٌ عَلَى شَرْحِ فِكْرَةٍ بَسِيطَةٍ
